title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (cote 140-3), Grothendieck's continuation of La Longue Marche. He is building Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type groups from a profinite group G^+. Judging from the neighbouring pages, G^+ is probably a cartographic or modular-type profinite group, with marked elements rho and sigma and subgroups L_0 and L_1 = rho(L_0).

Previous page. Z_{rho,sigma} is a group of quadruples (u, mu, eps, eps'), with u in Aut(G^+), mu in Zhat^*, and eps, eps' in {±1}. Presumably u sends rho and sigma to conjugates of rho^{±mu} and sigma^{±mu}, the signs being recorded by eps and eps'. The map l -> (int(l), 1, 1, 1) embeds L_0 into Z_{rho,sigma} with normal image. Injectivity rests on L_0 ∩ Cent(G^+) = {1}, which follows from L_0 ∩ L_1 = {1}; this is assumed in (15). Gamma_{rho,sigma} := Z/Im L_0 then plays the role of a 'rigidified Out' group, the analogue of GT. The point is that one quotients by the normalised inner part L_0 rather than by all inner automorphisms, much as in Drinfeld's normalised pairs (lambda, f).

This page.
(18) The projections (u, mu, eps, eps') -> mu, eps, eps' factor through Gamma. This gives a 'cyclotomic' character chi_Gamma : Gamma -> Zhat^* and two sign characters eps_Gamma, eps'_Gamma. Together they form Gamma -> Zhat^* × {±1} × {±1}.
(19)–(20) Their pullbacks to Z are just the coordinate projections.
Subgroups. He proposes Gamma° = ker(eps, eps') (orientation/sign-preserving part), Gamma^+ = ker chi (the 'geometric' part, chi = 1), Gamma^{°+} = their intersection, and Z°, Z^+, Z^{°+} for the preimages in Z.
3°) Z acts on G^+ through u, giving (21). He forms the semidirect product S_0G = Z ⋉ G^+ (22).

Next page. He divides by the antidiagonal copy of L_0, l -> (int l)·l^{-1}. This copy centralises G^+ and is normal. The quotient G_{rho,sigma} sits in an extension 1 -> G^+ -> G_{rho,sigma} -> Gamma_{rho,sigma} -> 1, compatible with 1 -> L_0 -> Z -> Gamma -> 1.

This is the standard construction of the extension of a 'Galois-type' group Gamma by the geometric fundamental group G^+, inducing the given outer action. It is the formal analogue of 1 -> pi_1^geom -> pi_1^arith -> Gal -> 1, here built over the abstract GT-like group Gamma_{rho,sigma} instead of Gal(Qbar/Q).
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The well-definedness of the quotient (24) on the next page needs Z to normalise L_0, compatibly with i_{L_0,Z}. This holds because int(u(l)) = u·int(l)·u^{-1} once u(L_0) = L_0, which is presumably part of the definition of Z_{rho,sigma} on earlier pages. With the right convention the antidiagonal map l -> (int l, l^{-1}) is indeed a homomorphism whose image centralises G^+.
The notation '+' for ker chi (rather than for an orientation-preserving part) is idiosyncratic but internally consistent.

ideas.what: Characters chi: Gamma -> Zhat^* and signs eps, eps' on a GT-type group of normalised automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of rho and sigma up to powers
ideas.modern_name: cyclotomic character on GT / sign characters on extended GT-type groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; for sign/orientation variants, cartographic-group work (e.g. Schneps et al.)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the action of Gal on profinite fundamental groups, but not these explicit formulas

ideas.what: Subgroups Gamma°, Gamma^+, Gamma^{°+} defined as kernels of the sign and cyclotomic characters
ideas.modern_name: kernels of characters; the 'geometric' part chi = 1 of GT-type groups

ideas.what: S_0G = Z ⋉ G^+ modulo the antidiagonal L_0, giving an extension of Gamma by G^+ with the prescribed outer action
ideas.modern_name: pushout extension inducing a given outer action (an analogue of the arithmetic fundamental group over GT)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory (extension theory with trivial obstruction); in the GT context, e.g. 'GT-analogue of pi_1 of the moduli stack' constructions

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up notation and a standard semidirect-product/quotient construction of an extension of a GT-like group by a profinite group. It is routine and has close analogues in the GT literature; at most it documents Grothendieck's own systematic set-up.
transcription_corrections: The group written 'gamma' in the machine text is Γ_{ρ,σ} (as on this page). The next page's transcription 'γ_γ' and the incomplete (28) should read χ_G = χ_Γ∘δ_G, ε_G = ε_Γ∘δ_G, ε'_G = ε'_Γ∘δ_G.
'Ĝ^+' on the previous page and '𝔊^+'/'𝔖^+' here and on the next page denote the same script group G^+.
Margin addition at 3°): 'Les groupes S_0G_{ρ,σ}, G_{ρ,σ}' replaces the struck-out line.
